summary: When the sample is only part of the matching trials, velocity takes recent_trials, prior_trials, later_trials, older_trials and the trial growth from four exact registry counts (one countTotal request per window) instead of from the sample, reports the origin in trial_counts_source, and falls back to the sample if any of the four requests fails.
reason: The first --sample trials are the API's default order, not a random draw, so they over-represent some years: for Long COVID the same equal windows read +11% from the 400-of-745 sample but +1% (346 vs 343) from the registry's exact counts. By-year buckets, enrollment and enrollment growth have no cheap exact equivalent and stay sample-based, and the note says so.
validated_outcome: Twelve mutations of the window logic each fail the new tests: a range ending or starting a year off, the later or older range bounded, the older range overlapping the prior window, exact counts never used, a partly exact result instead of all-or-nothing, a complete sample not recognised, a failed fetch not admitted, the condition dropped from the range request, ranges asked for without a registry total, and a note that always claims exact counts. An unchanged copy passes. Guarded by TestBuildVelocityViewUsesRegistryCounts, TestBuildVelocityViewFallsBackToSampleWhenARangeFails and TestVelocityNotes.
